title: Low-Dose STEM Characterizations of Halide Perovskite Photovoltaics’ Intragrain Defects, Interfaces and Evolutionary Behaviors
content: Halide perovskites (HPs) have emerged as promising semiconductor materials, garnering significant attention due to their exceptional optoelectronic properties and the potential for low-cost solar cell production through simple synthesis techniques. Despite these advantages, the operational longevity of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains inferior to that of their silicon counterparts [1]. Therefore, a thorough investigation into the structural causes of HP instability is imperative. Although state-of-the-art transmission electron microscopy (TEM) can elucidate structures at the atomic scale, the inherent instability of HPs under high-energy electron beam irradiation poses significant research challenges [2].
